passages.quote: Retraction: Detecting phishing websites using machine learning technique
The PLOS One Editors retract this article [1]
because it was identified as one of a series of submissions for which we have concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process
These concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results.
The author either did not respond directly or could not be reached.
The experiments' outcome shows that the proposed method's performance is better than the recent approaches in malicious URL detection.
passages.reason: Paper says method better than recent approaches.

passages.quote: The main evidence for our choice comes from Dutta [14], who built an RNN-LSTM URL detector, called LURL
passages.reason: Draft names Dutta as main evidence, LURL RNN-LSTM.

passages.quote: Therefore, the study proposes Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) based URL detection approach.
The proposed method (LURL) is developed in Python 3.0

and an F1-score of 96.4 on the Phishtank dataset [14]
LURL has produced an average of 97.4% and 96.8% for Phishtank and Crawler datasets respectively.
